newsitem.title: UK: Lehman survey shows funds switch to T-bonds, gilts.
newsitem.headline: Lehman survey shows funds switch to T-bonds, gilts.

text.p: International fund managers reduced their holdings of peripheral European bonds in February, with U.S. bonds and gilts benefiting, according to a survey by Lehman Brothers.

The survey of 38 managers of global bonds and currencies, managing $140 billion, showed that only 26 percent of investors said they were overweight of Italian bonds in February, compared with 39 percent in January.

"Peripheral positions in Europe have been cut," Lehman Brothers said in the survey. "Italian bonds have been reduced to July 1996 levels, (and) Spanish bond market exposure is lower than at any time in 1996."
It said Sweden was the favoured peripheral market.

The survey showed that there was a shift into U.S. bonds, more out of Japan than out of Europe. The pecentage of investors who said they were overweight U.S. bonds rose to 47 percent, from 22 percent in January.
Dollar positions rose to their highest level since September 1996, the survey showed, while European cross-currency positions have been reduced.
"Italian lira holdings are the lowest since the survey began," the statement said.
The number of investors overweight gilts increased to 57 percent, from 35 percent in January. -- International Bonds Unit +44 171 542 6137
